round: Series A (Kaszek-led, follow-on at Series C)
description: AI-driven plant-based food company (Giuseppe algorithm) building animal-product analogues — NotMilk, NotBurger, NotChicken — with a CPG distribution strategy across LATAM and the US. At Series A: a Chilean food-tech story riding the 2018 Beyond Meat momentum.
current_status: Pivoted from pure CPG to B2B AI licensing (Giuseppe platform). JV with Kraft Heinz handles US/Canada retail. Profitable in Chile, Argentina, Colombia, Peru as of Q2 2025. Targeting overall profitability by end 2026. Revenue ~$250M. Valuation $1.5B. CTO says bulk of future revenue will come from B2B licensing, not food sales.

founder.name: Matías Muchnick + Karim Pichara
founder.background: Muchnick: food-industry family roots, Harvard MBA — domain depth in CPG. Pichara: AI/ML PhD, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile computer-science professor, built the Giuseppe molecular-AI platform that is the technical core of NotCo.
founder.problem_fit: EXCEPTIONAL pairing: the domain + hard-science combination that most food-tech lacks. Muchnick knows how CPG really works; Pichara owns the AI advantage that can't be hired in.
founder.execution_evidence: Launched in 5 LATAM countries, landed JV with Kraft Heinz, pivoted cleanly from pure CPG to a B2B AI licensing model when category collapsed.
founder.red_flags: None material. The pivot execution proved adversity-tested.

stage_context.vs_base: Plant-based category momentum (2018 Beyond Meat IPO) suggested thriving/breakout upside, but CPG gross-margin reality and LATAM-DTC hybrid distribution pulled most-likely tier down to surviving (+8pp vs base). Dead and breakout tiers both below base — a cash-efficient AI-platform story, unlikely to die, unlikely to 100x.

verdict: NotCo survives IF (a) B2B Giuseppe licensing revenue exceeds 40% of total by 2027, (b) LATAM core stays gross-margin positive through inflation cycles, (c) Kraft Heinz JV produces net cash to the parent within 18 months. Most fragile: (a) — licensing AI to CPG incumbents requires them to admit they need the technology, which contradicts their brand equity.
top_risk: CPG unit economics: plant-based category growth stalled globally 2023-2025; pricing premium vs dairy/meat is eroding
top_opportunity: Giuseppe as a B2B AI platform (formulation-as-a-service) is a software margin business trapped inside a CPG cost structure — unlock is a spin-out
actual_outcome: Plant-based category collapse in 2023-2024 (Beyond Meat -80%, Oatly -85%) hit NotCo's retail DTC thesis hard. Company executed the pivot the verdict anticipated: shutdown of owned US operations, Kraft Heinz JV for distribution, and leaning into B2B AI. Valuation last reported at $1.5B (down from peak but not a down-round yet). Survival looks likely; unicorn-scale exit is not.
